answer: A hotel that genuinely exceeded my expectations was a resort in Cox's Bazar where I stayed during a family holiday by the sea, about a year after I started working. It was the first holiday I had helped to pay for, so it felt quite special, and the whole family came, including my elder sister, her husband and their two children. We stayed for four nights in December, when the weather is cool and dry. From the moment we arrived, the service was [[impeccable]], and the staff [[went out of their way]] to make us feel welcome, even arranging a small cake when they found out it was my mother's birthday. The room was spacious and immaculately clean, with a balcony overlooking the ocean, which was [[breathtaking]] at sunrise. What impressed me most was the attention to detail; everything felt thoughtfully designed and genuinely [[luxurious]] without being pretentious. The food was excellent, especially the seafood at dinner, and the whole atmosphere was wonderfully relaxing. I remember spending hours by the pool with my nephew, feeling completely at ease, while my parents walked on the beach. Of course, it was not cheap, but the experience felt [[worth every penny]]. Honestly, a well-run hotel can make or break a holiday, and this one made ours truly special. It set a standard that has been hard to match since. I still remember that stay as one of the most comfortable of my life.

followUps.q: Do you usually stay in hotels when you travel?
followUps.answer: Not usually. On most trips I stay with relatives or in cheaper guesthouses to save money, so that resort was a real treat. It was worth it once, but I could not afford that every time.

followUps.q: What do you think makes a good hotel?
followUps.answer: Friendly, attentive staff most of all, followed by cleanliness and comfort. A beautiful building helps, but if the staff are rude or careless, even the most luxurious hotel will not feel welcoming.

note: Set in Cox's Bazar with the whole family (elder sister, husband, two children); added when and how long, birthday detail; plain marks 'relaxing' and 'match' replaced by 'impeccable' and 'went out of their way', added 'worth every penny'.
